L6.1.quote: Claim. $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$ is the increasing enumeration of $S_\infty\cap[a_1,\infty)$.
L6.1.note: Step 1 proves both directions for every integer at least a_1.

L6.2.quote: *Claim 3.2 (self-dual).* Every minimal transversal of the family $\mathcal C$ belongs to $\mathcal C$. *Proof.* Let $T$ be a minimal (under inclusion) transversal of $\mathcal C$... Hence $\pi(T)\in S_\infty$
L6.2.note: T may be infinite, so pi(T) is undefined; the required self-duality and hence finiteness are not proved.

L6.3.note: Given finitely many minimal elements, Step 2 correctly proves periodicity from the first term.

parsed.notes: The characterization and conditional periodicity assembly are valid. The finiteness argument fails because an inclusion-minimal transversal of an intersecting family of finite sets need not be finite, yet Claim 3.2 applies pi(T) without proving finiteness.
